Close the last open collapse findings on PR 469 (branch `feat/collapse-large-sources-by-default`, trail 405, change 267), which blocks the whole stack. Start from `origin/feat/collapse-large-sources-by-default` (`git fetch origin` first; main now includes 468/471/473/474 so merge `origin/main` if it is behind); commit locally; I push. Read /Users/gabe/Projects/caliper-fixtures/worker-contract.md, /Users/gabe/Projects/caliper-fixtures/pr/fix-collapse-picked-notable.md (what the last round fixed and the stated limits) and crates/core/src/types/semantic.rs (checker_sources, Layering, keeps, move_notable), crates/semantic/src/convert.rs (picked), resolver/alias.rs.
Open findings (same family, repeated on 6 changes): (A) `Pick<PropsOf<typeof Widget>, Keys>` (and a project alias whose whole body is a Pick) selecting more than 200 members from a source that ONLY the checker reads is collapsed, hiding explicitly selected props. Last round fixed it where the structural lane reads the base or the checker records `picked`, but not for a named alias over a checker-only base: TypeScript names the type by the alias and the lib writes Omit as Pick<T, Exclude<keyof T, K>>, so the mapped type alone cannot tell Pick from Omit. Entire's new copy on change 281: 'when a conditional props type such as PropsOf<typeof Widget> exposes a large source ... (types/semantic.rs:653)'. (B2) Entire on change 277 (finding 01M7GP00RW3J, semantic.rs:450-451): filtering by member name alone can hide a prop declared by another, uncollapsed source.
Principle to apply (state it in your notes): the project rule is 'never hide on silence' (ADR 0028, 1e4a5283): when the checker cannot prove that nothing was selected away, the source must not be collapsed. So implement ONE rule in the single collapse decision: a source is collapsible only when the lane can show the props type reaches ALL of its members (no Pick/Omit/mapped selection between the source and the component, as known from the checker's own answer for the component's props type: e.g. its props type is the interface/class itself or an intersection with it), and `picked`/provenance are unknown => not collapsed (listed, bounded). Find what the checker (tsrs) can report to decide this without the Pick-vs-Omit ambiguity: the alias symbol, whether the type is a mapped/instantiated alias, or the declared members' count vs reaching count (the reaching count is computed after filtering, so a selection that reaches fewer than all members of the source shows as reaching < declared; use that if the declared count is available without new RPC machinery; the earlier declared-count machinery was deleted as dead, so prefer reasoning from what the answer already carries). If no sound signal exists, say so and choose: do not collapse a checker-only source when the props type is an alias or mapped application (listed, never wrong). Fix B2 by attributing by (source, key), not by key alone. Cost check: report how many components on the five corpora (chakra-only, gate-large, shadcn-ui, mantine, spectrum, antd if cheap) change from collapsed to listed (they must stay few; Chakra Button must remain ~146 argTypes), and peak RSS on chakra-only before/after (use /usr/bin/time -l; the memory rule). Tests first, in crates/semantic/tests/collapse_model.rs (the 300+ case model; add generators for: Pick over big checker-only source via alias, via direct, Omit, intersection, conditional PropsOf; same-named member in another source), each failing on base. Gates: `just lint doc-check machete typos`, nextest core+semantic+cli, `just test-checker-lane` (symlink target/release in your worktree to your CARGO_TARGET_DIR/release; CALIPER_BIN is ignored), identity diff on the five corpora explaining every difference. Then `/code-review medium` on your commits (explicit SHA range), one fix round; notes to /Users/gabe/Projects/caliper-fixtures/pr/fix-collapse-never-hide-on-silence.md (## What, ## Evidence, ## Not verified, session URL line). Own CARGO_TARGET_DIR under /Users/gabe/Projects/caliper-fixtures/shrink/, rust 1.99.1 first on PATH (/Users/gabe/.rustup/toolchains/1.99.1-aarch64-apple-darwin/bin). Cap 100 tool calls. ## What

Fixes the two Entire findings on PR 469 (trail 405, change 267). Both came from the same pattern: the collapse decision and the notable move were made with too little input (A: whether a `Pick` selected the keys; B: the notable state of layers the entry already has), and the two lanes did not share it.

- Finding A: the checker now reports the keys each lib `Pick` on the props type selects (`SemanticComponent::picked`, found in the same walk as `composes`). The merge does not count these keys toward a source's size and does not put them in a layer, so they stay listed. The structural lane already lists everything under a `Pick`.
- Finding B: a notable member of a collapsed layer the structural pass already made (`className`) is merged over its structural entry (the code default, the checker's type), then moved back to `notableInherited`. This applies only when both the checker's prop and the structural notable come from that layer's source. A notable member the structural answer lists itself (`Pick<Big, 'className'> & Omit<Big, 'x'>`) stays a prop.
- The same gap in the structural lane: destructuring defaults now reach a collapsed source's notable props, and `Partial`/`Required` set their optionality.

## Evidence

- `crates/semantic/tests/collapse_model.rs`:
  - `finding_a_…` and `finding_b_…` failed on 6b9a187b and pass now.
  - The `PickedAndLayered` and named-alias `Pick` cases were added failing and pass now. The exception is the checker-only named alias, a known limit (see below).
- `just lint doc-check machete typos`: exit 0.
- `cargo nextest run -p caliper-docgen-core -p caliper-docgen-semantic`: exit 0.
- `just test-checker-lane`: exit 0. It reads the binary from `target/release` (linked to my build).
- Full-content identity diff, `extract --json --quiet --no-cache`, base 6b9a187b vs head, JSON parsed and `stats` dropped:
  - gate-large, chakra-only, mantine core and react-spectrum are identical.
  - shadcn-ui differs in exactly one field: `notableInherited.onClick` in 60 components.
  - Why: `onClick` belongs to a collapsed `GlobalDOMEvents` layer from `@react-types/shared`, which the structural pass made. It now carries the checker's answer, `(event: MouseEvent<HTMLDivElement, MouseEvent>) => void`, instead of the structural `MouseEventHandler<HTMLDivElement>`. This is fix B taking effect: the checker lane now gives the checker's type, as it does for listed props. Parent, required and description are unchanged.

## Not verified

- nextest for the cli crate locally: the config tests need `tsx`, which is not installed in this worktree. CI runs them.
- A `Pick` that is the whole body of a project alias (`type P = Pick<Base, …>`) over a base only the checker reads is still collapsed in the checker lane.
  - Why: TypeScript names the type by the project alias, and the lib writes `Omit` as a `Pick`, so the mapped type alone cannot tell the two apart.
  - Where the structural lane reads the base, both lanes agree (tested).
- `picked` holds names, not (source, name). A member of another source with a picked key's name is left out of that source's count and layer. The worst case is that the prop is listed, never hidden; at the threshold that source can be listed instead of collapsed.
- The checker answers `""` for every property's JSDoc in a .ts file. `the_checker_answers_a_props_jsdoc` shows this and is `#[ignore]`d.
  - This also happens on base. tsrs 0.24 `getDocumentationComment` returns empty strings; the root cause inside tsrs was not found.
  - The merge hides it wherever the structural pass has a description. A source only the checker reads has none.
- Open review items, not fixed:
  - Destructuring defaults still do not reach HTML-layer notables (curated `type = 'button'`) or the synthesized `ref`. Fixing that changes output on the corpora.
  - The B merge needs the checker's `parent` to equal the layer's source exactly. A symlinked or re-exported path falls back to the structural entry.
  - `picked` also collects keys of a `Pick` nested inside an `Omit` or inside a dependency's own types.
  - Cost:
    - linear `picked.contains`;
    - `composes` keeps walking past unknown bases;
    - one extra `properties` call per `Pick`.
  - The doc claims that applying `layer_checker_props` twice gives the same result; that no longer holds without a merge in between.

# Worker contract (caliper). Read once; the brief only names the task, the files you own and the call cap.

Scope
- Edit only the files the brief names. If another file must change, stop and say which and why.
- Never ask the user questions. If blocked, report what blocks and what you tried. Do not wait on background work: finish or report.

Branch and push
- Branch from origin/main unless the brief says otherwise. Own CARGO_TARGET_DIR under ~/Projects/caliper-fixtures/<task>/. Scratch there too, never /tmp.
- Rust 1.99.1 on PATH (/Users/gabe/.rustup/toolchains/1.99.1-aarch64-apple-darwin/bin) for builds; commits need MISE_RUST_VERSION=1.99.1 (the mise shim forces 1.98.1). Caveat: with the toolchain bin first on PATH `rust-objcopy` can fail and strip silently does nothing; irrelevant unless you measure binary size.
- Signed commits ending `Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_013R2ytvK9B32ZaSUaSe6aAZ`. Push normally (`git push origin HEAD:<branch>`), never --no-verify, verify the remote SHA with `git ls-remote`. Do not open or edit the PR, do not poll CI.

Checks: targeted, CI runs the rest
- Always, before push: `just lint doc-check machete typos` (fast).
- Then only what your change touches: Rust -> nextest of the touched crates; types/output/merge -> `just test-checker-lane` once; checker/session code -> gate_harness determinism and memory modes; output-preserving change -> full-content diff (JSON parsed, `stats` dropped) of `extract --json --quiet --no-cache` vs a build of origin/main on ~/Projects/caliper-fixtures/gate-large/src and ~/Projects/caliper-fixtures/checker-default/chakra-only/src (tools: ~/Projects/caliper-fixtures/perf-analysis/same.py, identity.sh; ~/Projects/caliper-fixtures/final-perf/ab.sh interleaves two binaries).
- Do NOT run deny, semver, test-ts, test-napi, test-integration, test-py unless you changed those areas: CI runs them on every PR.
- Tests that fail on base for every behavior change. No oracle runs, no corpus fetches. No new scripts, options or recipes. Changeset only if `just semver` demands one.
- No wall-clock timing unless the brief asks; check `uptime`, and prefer allocation or instruction counts (load-independent).

Cap
- Stop and report after the call cap in the brief (default 60 tool calls) with what you have verified. Listing something as 'not done' with its cause beats burning more calls.

Artifacts (agents to agents; humans see them at the edge)
- Write the PR body to ~/Projects/caliper-fixtures/pr/<branch, slashes as dashes>.md: `## What`, `## Evidence` (numbers, exit codes, what was diffed), `## Not verified`, last line `https://claude.ai/code/session_013R2ytvK9B32ZaSUaSe6aAZ`. The lead publishes it unedited.
- Final message <= 120 words: branch, head SHA (ls-remote verified), body path, blockers. Nothing else.
